At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.description:
About The Role

GFL is seeking a visionary, high-energy leader with a passion for financial modeling, advanced analytics, and commercial business insights. Are you a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of complex data, technology, and executive strategy? As the Director of Business Analytics, you will drive our enterprise-wide intelligence roadmap and foster a high-impact, data-driven culture across our fast-paced, high-growth organization.

This is a newly created position driven by our consistent expansion, appetite for data-driven decision-making, and relentless push for continuous improvement. You will join our leadership team at an exceptionally exciting time as we’ve embarked on our pricing program transformation, placing you at the forefront of this value creating engagement. Working with a "no can't do" attitude, you will translate complex technical data into compelling commercial narratives that shape global corporate strategy and optimize bottom-line performance.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting directly to the VP, Operations Strategy, you will lead a dynamic team to drive performance and deliver value-added decision support across the business. Key responsibilities include:

Pricing Excellence: Assess enterprise pricing performance, build advanced pricing models from scratch, identify margin opportunities, and challenge assumptions. Influence Area Vice Presidents and Business Unit leaders to translate analytical insights into actionable strategies that optimize commercial outcomes.
Advanced Analytics & AI: Champion statistical modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics to transition the business from descriptive reporting to prescriptive intelligence. Accelerate speed-to-insight by integrating modern analytics tools, AWS-native workflows, predictive machine learning, and responsible GenAI/copilots.
Strategic Roadmap Development: Define and execute the long-term vision for the Business Analytics department. Scale enterprise data platforms and ensure full alignment between analytics initiatives and global corporate objectives.
Operational Excellence: Oversee the full data lifecycle—from ingestion and pipeline collaboration to the delivery of interactive executive dashboards, automated workflows, and high-impact predictive tools.
Data Governance & Integrity: Establish rigorous standards for data quality, security, and governance. Define control frameworks and KPIs to ensure business intelligence is accurate, reliable, and meeting compliance benchmarks.
Stakeholder Influence: Partner closely with Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Finance leadership. Translate ambiguous operational and market questions into clear recommendations, guiding executive partners through trade-offs with decision-ready narratives.
Team Leadership: Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of analysts and data professionals. Foster a culture of continuous improvement, analytical rigor, and collaborative business partnering.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive experience in analytics, data science, or related quantitative fields, including experimentation frameworks, statistical modeling, and time-series analysis.
5+ years in pricing, revenue management, or applied data science within B2B or service-oriented industries, with a proven track record of building dynamic pricing and financial models from scratch.
5+ years of people management experience, including structuring team processes for service delivery in fast-paced environments, presenting to C-suite audiences, and driving cross-functional alignment.
Expert-level modeling skills and hands-on proficiency with major BI tools (Power BI, QuickSight, Tableau) and database querying (SQL).
Direct experience with AWS cloud data environments (e.g., S3, Glue, Athena, Forecast, or SageMaker) and leveraging GenAI/copilots to accelerate insight generation.
Executive Communication & Influence: Exceptional ability to distill complex data insights into concise, persuasive presentations for senior leaders.
Commercial & Financial Acumen: Deep understanding of operational finance, FP&A, and business operations, with the ability to link data metrics directly to bottom-line profitability.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or Computer Science required; Master’s degree in a quantitative field highly preferred.

Drive continuous improvement initiatives and develop efficient and effective processes and procedures;

Develops options through the oversight of complex financial analysis and modelling. Reviews and analyzes organizational financial performance to provide advice to the leadership that enables effective decision making.
Develops financial procedures with the Controller and implements them in a complex and dynamic environment.
Acts as functional lead on projects to develop or redesign processes and procedures to increase efficiencies and to ensure effective internal controls for enterprise risk management.

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture and the standards that make data machine-readable for AI agents and operate the architecture function with agents as a core part of how it works. Success means fewer data stores and point-to-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.

Key pillars of this role:

Agent Assisted Architecture operations: Run continuous inventory of data platforms and stores across RBC’s stacks. Deploy automated architecture review and decision record workflows powered by agents to scale governance and documentation
Agent governance and trust: Establish audit trails of agent data access tied to entitlements. Implement evals to validate whether agents can answer correctly from data products. Define human-in-the-loop thresholds and ensure agents meet regulatory expectations for auditability and transparency

What will you do?

Manufacturing (data sources): Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source. Establish feedback loops where agent usage and failures feedback to producers-if agents can't interpret a field, that becomes a defect against the source.
Distribution (data platform architecture): Contribute to data distribution platform architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Operate a roadmap to retire point-to-point interfaces.
Agent-assisted architecture operations: Run continuous inventory of data platforms and stores across RBC's stacks. Deploy automated architecture review and decision record workflows powered by agents. Enable agents to assist in architecture assessment, governance documentation, and exception tracking at scale.
Discovery and machine readability: Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent-access pattern for data products, such as MCP. Include unstructured data (documents, emails, call transcripts) with appropriate chunking, embeddings and freshness strategies so retrieval-augmented workflows have high-quality context.
Consumption: Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
Agent governance and trust: Design and implement evals for data products to validate whether agents can answer correctly from them. Establish audit trails of agent data access tied to entitlements. Define human-in-the-loop thresholds and escalation patterns. Align with model-risk governance frameworks (OSFI E-23) to ensure agents operating on data products meet regulatory expectations for transparency and auditability.
Governance by design: Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support regulatory lineage and jurisdiction-aware data placement for sovereignty.
Data quality for retrieval: Establish quality standards and practices specific to retrieval scenarios: chunking strategies, freshness SLAs, embedding quality, and unstructured data preparation (documents, emails, call transcripts). Ensure that data products used in RAG and agent workflows meet standards for accuracy and interpretability.
Simplification and transformation: Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third-party rationalization. Track and communicate measurable outcomes: machine-readability coverage (% of critical data elements with semantics, owner, lineage and entitlements), agent task success rates on data products, and time-to-onboard new data products.
Build/buy stance on the agent layer: Establish strategy and standards for agent infrastructure: gateway and routing, tool registry for data product access, and shared context or memory layers. Make principled decisions on build versus buy for agent-specific data infrastructure.

What do you need to succeed?

15+ years in data architecture or data engineering, including 5+ years leading architects at enterprise scale.
Depth across lakehouse and warehouse platforms, streaming and CDC, data products and mesh, catalogs and metadata, semantic layers and knowledge graphs.
A track record of measurable simplification and modernization: data feeds rationalized, costs reduced, machine-readability coverage improved and agent task success rates on data products demonstrated.
Working knowledge of regulatory frameworks including BCBS 239, privacy regulation, OSFI E-23 (model risk) and OSFI expectations for data risk.
Clear view on making data AI-ready for retrieval, entitlement propagation, agent access and unstructured data workflows.
Experience designing and implementing data product governance, metadata standards and agent-accessible data architectures.
Able to align the CDO, platform engineering, business data owners and AI/ML leadership without direct authority over them.

What's in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. new_jobs.title: Vice-President Global Transaction Banking Sales
new_jobs.description:
National Bank of Canada is building a unified Global Transaction Banking (GTB) franchise that brings together transaction banking capabilities across Commercial Banking, National Client Group, Capital Markets, Product, Technology and Operations. Together, these platforms serve an expanding base of domestic and global clients across their working-capital and treasury lifecycles.
GTB’s ambition is to accelerate quality deposit growth, deepen primary client relationships, increase transaction banking revenues and deliver a differentiated, scalable and client-led experience.
As Vice-President, Global Transaction Banking Sales, Commercial and National Client Group, you will lead the GTB sales franchise across Commercial Banking, including specialized sectors such as Real Estate, Technology, Creative Industries and Equipment Finance, as well as the National Client Group. You will play a pivotal role in shaping GTB’s next phase of growth, with responsibility for go-to-market strategy, business development, sales execution and the mobilization of coverage teams across the franchise.
You will translate GTB’s strategy into clear segment priorities, market propositions and commercial plans; identify where the Bank can win; and build the disciplines, connectivity and talent required to convert opportunity into sustainable deposits, revenue and client primacy.
This position could be based anywhere in Canada.
Your Job

Own and execute the GTB sales Deposit and Cash Management strategy for Commercial Banking and National Client Group, translating enterprise priorities into clear go-to-market plans by client segment, industry, geography and relationship tier.
Build and continually refine the GTB Deposit and Cash Management commercial proposition, including the client value proposition, coverage model, referral pathways, sales plays and market activation agenda.
Lead business-development agenda by identifying priority markets, sectors, prospects and client opportunities; setting target lists; and establishing disciplined account and pursuit plans.
Drive the origination and conversion of deposits, cash management, payments, liquidity, working capital and broader transaction banking opportunities, with a clear focus on share of wallet, primary-bank relationships and sustainable relationship economics.
Mobilize Commercial Banking and National Client Group relationship teams around GTB priorities, equipping them with the tools, training, messaging and specialist support required to originate and advance opportunities.
Serve as senior sponsor for complex and strategic opportunities, leading executive-level client dialogue, pitches, negotiations and internal alignment from opportunity identification through implementation and revenue realization.
Partner closely with the Capital Markets & Public Sector GTB sales leaders, Trade Finance, FIG, Commercial Banking, Global Markets, Wealth Management and other coverage teams to coordinate cross-franchise opportunities and deliver consistent client experience.
Work with Product, Technology, Operations, Treasury, Risk, Legal and Compliance to ensure that market needs and client feedback inform the product roadmap, technology priorities, operating model and service experience.
Establish a disciplined sales-management and performance framework, including pipeline governance, forecasting, conversion metrics, sales capacity, client coverage, revenue, deposit and share-of-wallet KPIs.
Apply disciplined pricing and relationship economics, balancing client value, deposit characteristics, liquidity, funding objectives, risk appetite and total relationship profitability.
Represent GTB and the Bank with senior clients, industry associations and external stakeholders, strengthening market visibility, connectivity and the Bank’s reputation as a strategic transaction banking partner.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing national sales organization, including talent strategy, role clarity, succession, performance management and a culture of accountability, collaboration and client ownership.
Contribute to GTB’s broader strategic agenda, including business cases, investment priorities, partnerships, market expansion and the evolution of a scalable end-to-end transaction banking franchise.

Your Team

You will be a member of the GTB National Sales leadership team and report to the Managing Director & Head – Global Transaction Banking Sales, Capital Markets & Commercial Banking, Ontario & Western Canada. The Vice-President has overall accountability for GTB sales, product and servicing; this role has dedicated accountability for sales across Commercial Banking and National Client Group for Ontario & Western Canada.
You will work closely with senior leaders across Commercial Banking, National Client Group, Capital Markets, Product, Technology, Operations, Treasury, Risk, Legal and Compliance. Success will depend on your ability to lead through a matrix, create shared accountability and turn the Bank’s collective capabilities into a coherent market proposition.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in finance, business administration or a related field; a graduate degree is an asset.
Approximately 12 to 15 years or more of relevant experience in transaction banking, treasury services, commercial or corporate banking, payments, cash management or a related financial-services discipline, including meaningful leadership responsibility.
A proven record of building businesses, developing go-to-market strategies, leading national or multi-region sales teams and delivering measurable growth in deposits, revenue, client primacy or share of wallet.
Strong understanding of Commercial Banking and National Client Group clients, their treasury needs and the role of deposits, payments, liquidity, cash management and working-capital solutions in deepening relationships.
Demonstrated ability to originate opportunities, build executive relationships, lead complex pursuits and convert market insight into commercially viable solutions.
Strong understanding of transaction banking economics, pricing, risk management, balance-sheet considerations and the broader Capital Markets and banking environment.
Exceptional executive communication, presentation, negotiation and stakeholder-influence skills, with the credibility to engage senior clients and internal leaders.
Entrepreneurial, commercially minded and strategic, with the energy and resilience to build a new franchise while maintaining disciplined execution.
Bilingualism is an asset for national coverage.
Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) or comparable designation is an asset.
Ability to travel nationally and, as required, internationally.

Success in the Role

A clear and differentiated GTB go-to-market strategy for Commercial Banking and National Client Group, translated into measurable segment and market plans.
Growth in quality deposits, transaction banking revenues, client share of wallet and primary banking relationships.
A healthy, visible and well-governed pipeline with improved origination, conversion and sales productivity.
Stronger connectivity between relationship teams, GTB specialists, Product, Capital Markets and other Bank partners.
Improved end-to-end client experience, from origination and solution design through onboarding, implementation and servicing.
A scalable national sales model, supported by strong talent, clear accountability, effective KPIs and a high-performance culture.
Meaningful contribution to the development of a differentiated, integrated and sustainable GTB franchise.

Required skills: Accountability, Agility, Capital Markets, Client-focused, Communication, Humility, Initiative, Interpersonal Skills, Leadership, Problem Solving, Sales, Teamwork
